page: Amazon Web Services r8g.24xlarge is a memory-optimized server powered by custom AWS Graviton Neoverse-V2 processors built on the arm64 architecture. The instance features 96 dedicated physical cores running at 2.8 GHz, with a single thread per core, and is managed via the Nitro hypervisor. It is equipped with 768.0 GB of system memory, yielding a ratio of 8.0 GB of RAM per core. The processor includes 64 KB of L1d cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 36 MB of L3 cache, with hardware support for AES cryptography. There is no local storage or GPU hardware bundled with this instance type. Baseline network bandwidth is rated at 40 Gbps.

Benchmark results indicate top-tier multi-core and memory subsystem capabilities. The server achieves top-decile performance in multi-core CPU stress tests, memory bandwidth (both cached small-block and uncached large-block reads and writes), and PassMark database operations. Redis SET operations reach 195.4 million operations per second, and static web serving throughput is also in the top tier. Single-core benchmarks, such as stress-ng single-core and Geekbench single-core, fall into the average tier. Large-model LLM inference text generation (7B and 70B models) performs in the top tier, while prompt processing speeds for these models remain in the average tier.

The arm64 architecture and high memory density provide qualitative cost efficiency for memory-intensive workloads compared to traditional x86 architectures. However, tradeoffs include the complete absence of local NVMe storage, requiring network-attached storage, and the lack of hardware accelerators like GPUs. The server is optimized for memory-bound applications, large-scale databases, Redis caching layers, software compilation, and medium-to-large LLM inference text generation.
description: Amazon Web Services r8g.24xlarge is a memory-optimized server powered by 96 dedicated physical cores on the arm64 AWS Graviton Neoverse-V2 processor, running at 2.8 GHz. It features 768.0 GB of RAM, providing 8.0 GB of memory per core, and operates on the Nitro hypervisor. The instance lacks local storage and GPU accelerators but delivers 40 Gbps of baseline network bandwidth. Benchmark data shows top-tier multi-core CPU performance, exceptional memory bandwidth, and high-throughput database and Redis operations, though single-core performance remains average. This profile makes the server highly efficient for memory-intensive workloads, including large-scale databases, caching layers, and text-generation tasks for medium and large language models, while presenting tradeoffs in local storage availability and single-threaded execution speeds.
